purpose: Force Pattern Lab to apply the mechanics seen in high-performing city-history, urbanism, construction, abandoned-place, and public-history channels without copying their creative work.
core_thesis: One city. One strange visual clue. One source trail. One hidden system.
style_target: Bright Sun Films mystery + The B1M polish + Not Just Bikes clarity + Here Grows New York map proof.

benchmark_channels.name: The B1M
benchmark_channels.mechanic_to_adapt: premium documentary polish, clear stakes, big visual proof

benchmark_channels.name: Bright Sun Films
benchmark_channels.mechanic_to_adapt: mystery-first place storytelling, real footage, what-happened-here framing

mandatory_rules: Sell a mystery, contradiction, vanished place, map change, or hidden system; never package as a generic History of X topic.
Open the first 5 seconds with a visible source/photo/map clue and contradiction before Pattern Lab branding.
Pay off the title and thumbnail promise within the first 30 seconds.
Use photo-first and source-grounded thumbnails with one city anchor, one proof object, one dominant focal point, and 2-4 words.
Keep visuals full of real people, buildings, attractions, neighborhoods, industry, maps, documents, newspapers, transit, aerials, and modern context footage that match the narration.
No full-screen slide-deck visuals, generic AI history imagery, fake archival proof, copied thumbnail layouts, or generic skyline-only packaging.
Create every Short as a standalone clue with a first-frame promise, proof/payoff, and bridge back to the long-form video.
Prepare a 5-7 Short concept pack for each long-form episode even when only the best 3 are rendered first.
Use YouTube title/thumbnail testing where available; choose winners by watch-time share and expectation-match comments, not taste alone.
After publishing, analyze CTR by surface, first-30-second retention, average view duration, subscribers per 1,000 views, city requests, source disputes, and Shorts-to-long clicks.
blocked_patterns: History of {city} as the primary title frame
generic skyline thumbnail without proof object
slide deck or vector graphic as the dominant visual grammar
AI-generated fake historical photo presented as evidence
thumbnail/title promise not shown in first 30 seconds
Shorts that are only trailers and not standalone clues
copying another channel's thumbnail layout or distinctive brand system
